title: PPG spectral tail mass improves external high-rate ranking but fails a two-cohort criterion with sparse source events
abstract: Integrated PPG respiratory spectral mass above24 breaths/min did not establish improved high-rate discrimination in both cohorts. Relative to dominant spectral rate, record-balanced AUROC increased by0.474 (95% record-bootstrap CI -0.274 to0.591) in BIDMC and0.159 (0.029 to0.322) in independent CapnoBase. Only3 BIDMC records contained positive windows. Both datasets were previously exposed; this is exploratory transport, not untouched confirmation or a clinical tachypnea detector.
